Pathway: A. Data in — how data gets into Meldra
Capability: Upload CSV / Excel (one file or sheet per system)
What exists today: Multiple files; each sheet a source; kept in the browser (50 MB) or, with the lakehouse on, uploaded straight into the Meldra lakehouse as Apache Iceberg tables (CSV, Excel, Parquet; tested with 5,000,000 rows / 203 MB: stored in 21 s)
Gap / what is missing: No refresh for files (re-upload to update)
Next action: None now
Customer value: Anyone can start in minutes with exports

Capability: Add a source from a database query (Postgres, MySQL, SQL Server; later Snowflake, Databricks, Oracle)
What exists today: Data sources > Connect a database (Postgres, MySQL, SQL Server): pick tables (Postgres foreign keys become links) or write a SELECT; read-only transaction; row cap. With the lakehouse on, results are stored as Iceberg tables and refreshed in place. Tested end to end against a real PostgreSQL 16 server with a read-only user (e2e/multisource).
Gap / what is missing: Snowflake, Databricks, Oracle drivers; scheduled refresh; saved connections (needs server storage decision UR-X1); foreign keys for MySQL/SQL Server; SQLite excluded on purpose (the existing SQLite option opens server file paths: security fix needed in Database Connection).
Next action: Add Snowflake (UR-A3) after UR-X1 is decided; fix the SQLite path issue in the existing Database Connection page

Capability: Generic REST / SOAP / GraphQL / OData connector with presets (SuccessFactors, S/4, Microsoft Graph, Workday RaaS, Salesforce, QuickBooks)
What exists today: Backend connector for REST/JSON, OData, GraphQL, SOAP; presets (SuccessFactors, S/4HANA/BTP, Microsoft Graph, Workday, Salesforce, QuickBooks, Stripe, Kyriba); token sign-in (OAuth 2.0 client credentials with secret or certificate, refresh token, JWT bearer, SAML 2.0 bearer) so no IP allowlisting; paging (OData, Link header, next URL, offset, page, cursor, after-last-ID); SSRF protection; credentials never stored. Tested live against a public internet API (npm registry, 2 pages) and against simulated identity providers that verify signatures.
Gap / what is missing: Not yet tried against a real SuccessFactors / Entra ID / Salesforce / Workday tenant; no mutual TLS; no scheduled refresh
Next action: One live check per system with a pilot customer
Customer value: Pull directly from HR / finance / CRM systems

Capability: Refresh a source on demand / on schedule
What exists today: On-demand refresh for database and API sources (credentials entered again), in the browser or in the lakehouse (table swapped, column choices kept)
Gap / what is missing: Scheduled refresh needs a credential vault
Next action: On-demand refresh first (re-run query/API with credentials entered again); scheduled after UR-X1

Capability: SAP BDC, Snowflake/Databricks native, Workday live, Intuit, AWS (S3/Athena)
Gap / what is missing: Partner programs needed for some (SAP BDC, Workday listing, Intuit app review)
Next action: Start partner applications once a pilot exists

Pathway: B. Unified model — how separate systems become one
Capability: Detect numbers, dates, money, IDs; choose role (breakdown / number / ignore); rename join names
What exists today: model.js profileColumns(); Data sources tab column editor
Gap / what is missing: Multi-currency not converted

Capability: Business columns shared by 2+ sources become join axes (department, customer, month…)
What exists today: model.js buildModel() shared
Gap / what is missing: No hierarchy (e.g. department → division), no calendar (quarter, fiscal year)
Next action: Add date hierarchy (month → quarter → year, fiscal year start setting)

Capability: Key links suggested from real value overlap; manual links; one source borrows another's columns
What exists today: model.js suggestRelationships()
Gap / what is missing: Only exact key matches; many-to-many not supported

Capability: Match the same customer / supplier / employee written differently ('BT Group' vs 'British Telecommunications plc')
What exists today: Was in the first prototype ('needs your decision' cards), removed when moving to real data
Gap / what is missing: No fuzzy matching or match review
Next action: Fuzzy matching on name + postcode/VAT/email, with a 'needs your decision' queue and a saved match table
Customer value: Correct totals across systems (the core promise)

Capability: Named business metrics defined once (revenue, headcount, cost per head, off-contract spend) and reused by everyone and by the AI
What exists today: Definitions exist only inside individual answers / dashboard tiles
Gap / what is missing: No shared definitions
Next action: Let users save an answer as a metric; AI picks saved metrics first
Customer value: Same question → same number every time

Capability: Save sources + links + metrics as a named workspace (e.g. 'Finance Q3')
What exists today: With the lakehouse on, sources live in Meldra and follow the account to any device; links, dashboard and answers still saved per browser
Gap / what is missing: Links, dashboards and metrics not yet stored server-side; one workspace per account
Next action: Store the workspace (links, dashboard, saved answers) next to the tables
Customer value: Separate projects per customer or team

Pathway: C. Asking — how people get answers
Capability: Questions generated from the user's own data (cross-source first)
What exists today: engine.js suggestQuestions()

Capability: AI planner (metadata only) → validated spec; rules fallback; clarifying questions; 'can't answer' with closest alternative
What exists today: unified_reporting_service.py; engine.js heuristic()
Gap / what is missing: Not yet verified with the production OpenAI key
Next action: Verify one typed question in production
Customer value: Ask like a person, not a BI tool

Capability: Visible filter chips on an answer (region = UK, year = 2026) that can be added/removed
What exists today: Filter bar on every answer (is / is not; month from / up to) applied to each source that has the column; dashboard-wide filters

Capability: This year vs last year, quarter-on-quarter, rolling 12 months, % change
What exists today: Prior-year and prior-month comparison with change %, rolling 3/6/12 months (averages recombined from raw totals), % of total; AI and rules planners understand them
Gap / what is missing: Quarter / fiscal-year grain (depends on UR-B2)
Next action: Add quarter and fiscal year

Capability: Click a bar → see the breakdown or the underlying rows
Next action: Click-to-drill into the next dimension and a row-level table (with source system)

Capability: 'How it's calculated': plain-English steps, SQL, editable definition, source row counts
What exists today: AnswerCard.jsx describe(), toSQL()

Next action: Covered by drill-down (UR-C5)

Pathway: D. Delivering — how answers are used
Capability: Bar, line, pie, table, KPI, bubble (x vs y vs z), second axis, chart switcher, CSV download
What exists today: Bar, line, area, bar+line combo, pie, treemap, funnel, radar, table, KPI, bubble, heatmap, waterfall, second axis, chart switcher; any chart named in a prompt is used; angled labels when crowded
Gap / what is missing: Maps, forecast lines
Next action: Forecast line with predictive work

Capability: Pin answers as live tiles
What exists today: Pin answers or a whole prompt-built report as live tiles; dashboard-wide filters; tiles over lakehouse data calculate on the server
Gap / what is missing: Not shareable; no layout editing
Next action: Resize/reorder tiles; one filter bar for the whole dashboard

Capability: Export an answer or dashboard to PowerPoint, PDF, Excel
What exists today: Excel export of an answer, a report or the whole dashboard (contents sheet + one sheet per chart, filters described); CSV per answer
Gap / what is missing: PowerPoint / PDF not yet
Next action: 'Export to PowerPoint' reusing the existing PPT service; Excel export of tables

Capability: Share a dashboard with colleagues (link, roles)

Next action: Share read-only snapshot link first (no live data), then live sharing

Capability: Weekly email of a dashboard; alert when a number crosses a threshold
Gap / what is missing: Needs stored credentials + server jobs — see UR-X1
Next action: After UR-X1 and UR-A4

Capability: Data processed in the browser; AI sees metadata only
What exists today: AI sees metadata only; browser data deleted on logout; with the lakehouse: one Iceberg namespace per account, identifiers validated server-side, deletes remove every data/metadata file (verified), no connector secrets stored
Gap / what is missing: Object-store encryption and retention rules are deployment settings; no audit log of who ran which query
Next action: Clear-on-logout + optional passphrase encryption (secureLocalStore.js exists)

Capability: Roles (viewer / builder / admin), row-level security
Gap / what is missing: Needs UR-X1
Next action: Design with UR-X1

Capability: Freshness per source, rows matched vs unmatched in links, blanks warning
What exists today: Row counts per source; '(blank)' groups explained
Gap / what is missing: No freshness date, no link match-rate on answers
Next action: Show 'as of' date and link match % on every answer
Customer value: Users know when to trust a number

Capability: Meldra lakehouse: sources as Apache Iceberg tables, Apache Polaris catalog, Apache Arrow + DuckDB aggregation
What exists today: app/services/lakehouse, /api/lakehouse/*: streamed ingest (flat memory), typing identical to the browser, one namespace per account, server-side aggregation returning the same accumulators as the browser (parity-tested on 12 answer types), link suggestions over full tables, full-file deletion. 5M rows: stored in 21 s, answered in 0.4 s. Tested on SQL catalog and a real Apache Polaris 1.3 server.
Gap / what is missing: Partitioning by month; Polaris deployment on Railway; per-query cost limits; sharing between users of an organisation
Next action: Deploy Polaris + S3/R2; switch tenant to organisation id for shared workspaces
Customer value: Handles enterprise data volumes; data follows the user

Capability: Build a whole report from one prompt; AI picks charts from column names only; rules take over without AI
What exists today: "Build a report" in the composer: up to 8 charts (KPI, trends, breakdowns, cross-system), add all to dashboard, Excel export; rule-based report prefers pairs from different systems
Gap / what is missing: AI quality not yet measured on real customer data
Next action: Collect prompts from pilots and tune the report prompt

Capability: File + real PostgreSQL + live public API combined in the UI, numbers checked against the sources
What exists today: e2e/multisource: 16 checks, all passing; e2e/lakehouse: 29 checks; e2e/connector-auth: 19 checks

Capability: Where data lives: browser-only (today) vs encrypted server-side workspace

Capability: First target persona and 3 flagship questions
